question: Failure and remedy: when it breaks, who can freeze, who pays, who decides?
answer: For 18 of the 36 crypto dollars the library tracks, the issuer can freeze or block coins; for 15 the terms read do not say. When a firm collapsed, customers were being paid back at least partly in 3 of the 10 cases on the International Crypto Map, and courts decided whether customer crypto was the customer's property or the estate's. The 7 programmable-payment failures were corrected by forks, freezes or restitution, not one rule. 37 of 41 U.S. jurisdictions in the register have enacted UCC Article 12, the law on who owns a controllable electronic record.

rows.title: Cryptopia liquidation

badges.text: Partly paid back in crypto

cells: Exchange liquidated 14 May 2019 after a hack and asset loss
Wallet-to-wallet distributions began December 2024, up to 90% for an eligible BTC/DOGE subset; later phases continue
Liquidators reconciled asset-specific crypto trusts; approximately 17 BTC recovered by the FBI was available for further tracing
High Court held cryptocurrency is property held on trust and approved distribution directions
Stolen assets, low-value trusts, unclaimed holdings, costs and claim gates prevent a universal 100% statement
Trust property and executed wallet transfers support a concrete partial return, not complete recovery for every account holder or coin.

rows.title: Mt. Gox civil rehabilitation

badges.text: Partly paid back

cells: Exchange failure and loss followed by a Tokyo District Court-confirmed rehabilitation plan
Bitcoin and Bitcoin Cash repayments reached more than 19,500 creditors by 27 March 2025; remaining repayments continue
Rehabilitation trustee controls estate crypto and cash; designated exchanges act as receipt agents
Creditor status, selected repayment method, verified account and plan conditions govern entitlement
Base, early lump-sum and intermediate repayment deadline extended to 31 October 2026
Trustee delivery through an agent is a court-plan repayment, not reversal of the original blockchain loss.

rows.title: FTX Chapter 11 distribution

badges.text: Being paid back in cash

cells: Multinational exchange-group claims in U.S. bankruptcy
Cash distribution program is operating; 31 July 2026 was scheduled for qualifying allowed claims and a customer dashboard records individual status
Recovery Trust and plan administrator marshal cash and reserves and send U.S. dollars to approved distribution providers
Confirmed plan distinguishes allowed and disputed claims; KYC, tax, sanctions, jurisdiction and onboarding gates apply
USD6.5 billion disputed-claims reserve; claims can be deferred or forfeited when conditions remain unmet
U.S. venue does not make every debtor or creditor American; dollar delivery and any later token purchase are separate transactions.

rows.title: Hodlnaut liquidation

badges.text: Payout pending

cells: Interim judicial management 29 August 2022; liquidation 10 November 2023
First-interim-dividend proof and adjudication process active in 2026; public bundle does not yet prove creditor receipt
Liquidators realize group assets, litigation claims, seized-crypto claim and FTX distributions
Users are creditors; proofs of debt for dividend purposes require separate adjudication from voting claims
Approximately SGD389.7 million of claims admitted for voting at 30 September 2025; timing and quantum remain dependent on realization and adjudication
An estate recovery, including from FTX, is not a Hodlnaut user distribution until the dividend reaches an admitted creditor.

rows.title: JPEX investigation and prosecution

badges.text: Nothing paid back

cells: 2023 withdrawal complaints and alleged balance changes after unlicensed promotion
No official customer distribution or restitution series located
Police reported HKD228 million frozen, including about HKD14.5 million of crypto, by 28 February 2025
2,636 reports and 1,311 statements; sixteen suspects charged in November 2025; charges are not convictions
HKD1.616 billion reported amount cannot be netted against frozen assets as a recovery rate
Investigation, freezing and charging are separate from adjudicated entitlement, forfeiture and customer cash receipt.

rows.title: X AG stablecoin enforcement

badges.text: Outcome not public

cells: One of two bank default guarantees fell away, leaving full repayment no longer assured
Actual redemptions, customer receipt and distribution withheld
Issuer and guarantor arrangement described; token, balances and reserve composition withheld
FINMA found unlawful public deposits and issued a final restoration and cessation decision on 16 December 2025
Liquidation threatened for noncompliance; identity and customer outcome remain confidential
The case proves a structural guarantee failure, not the token identity, size of customer loss or recovery distribution.

rows.title: QuadrigaCX bankruptcy

badges.text: Large shortfall

cells: Exchange customer assets and internal balances
Platform fraud, false balances and trading losses; creditor protection 5 February 2019
Asset recovery and identification established; this bundle does not claim a final customer payout rate
Monitor/trustee recovered or identified about CAD46 million across bank funds, drafts, processors and settlement assets
Bankruptcy claims govern distribution; OSC report is staff fact-finding and was not court-tested
CAD215 million owed and CAD169 million estimated shortfall
Recovered or identified estate assets are not the same as cash received by customers and do not erase the shortfall.

rows.title: Mirror Trading International

badges.text: Order, no cash recovered

cells: Fraudulent bitcoin commodity pool and pyramid scheme
Provisional liquidation December 2020; final liquidation June 2021
Restitution order entered; no matching collected-and-paid customer total established
South African liquidators control the estate; court record says more than ZAR1 billion of bitcoin was held at liquidation
South African court declared the scheme unlawful and agreements void; U.S. court imposed more than USD1.7 billion restitution
CFTC expressly warns that payment orders may not yield recovery when wrongdoers lack assets
A liability and restitution figure is not a distribution receipt or a measure of assets available in the South African estate.

rows.title: Wuhan virtual-currency cash-out fraud

badges.text: Fully recovered

cells: One virtual-currency transfer and linked CNY cash obligation
Counterparties denied receiving the token transfer and withheld CNY200,000 equivalent
Police reported the victim's CNY200,000 loss fully recovered
Police technical analysis verified the virtual currency reached the specified account
Suspects confessed and were criminally detained; investigation remained active
One local case does not establish a national recovery rate
Recovery of the fiat loss did not reverse the original blockchain transfer or license the underlying trade.

rows.title: MiCA transition wind-down comparator

badges.text: Orderly exit, not a failure

cells: Former DASP registration without successor MiCA authorization
French transition ended 1 July 2026 for providers without MiCA authorization
Exit access required; no loss or distribution is implied
Provider had to permit customer transfer or sale during orderly cessation
AMF administrative authorization and removal process, not insolvency adjudication
Removal proves registry state only, not solvency, successful withdrawals or zero customer loss
An orderly regulatory exit is a correction-control comparator, not evidence that a firm failed or every customer exited successfully.

rows.title: Custodia Bank v. Federal Reserve Board & FRB Kansas City — D. Wyo.; 10th Cir. 24-8024; SCOTUS No. 26-62
cells: Does statutory eligibility give a state-chartered bank a right to a Reserve Bank master account?

Tenth Circuit (2025-10-31): eligibility for a master account is not an entitlement. Custodia petitioned the Supreme Court on 2026-07-10 (No. 26-62); the Fed opposed review on 2026-10-13. The Court has not yet decided whether to hear it.

THE gate case. Every crypto bank, fintech trust, and state money experiment needs the Fed's rails; whether access is a right or a favor is now before the Court — or settled for a generation if cert is denied.

cells: Must a Reserve Bank serve a state-chartered cannabis credit union?
Fractured 1-1-1 judgment; amended lawful-purpose complaint allowed; no entitlement established. Later Custodia law rejects the entitlement reading.
The first crack at the gate question — three judges, three theories, no rule — showing why Custodia's published holding matters.

rows.title: Lacewell (NYDFS) v. OCC — S.D.N.Y.; 2d Cir. 19-4271 (2021)
cells: May the OCC charter a national bank that takes no deposits (the fintech charter)?
Merits vacated for ripeness — OCC never issued the charter, so its authority remains legally unresolved.
The unanswered question under every new OCC trust and stablecoin charter: nobody yet knows if the nondepository national charter survives a merits fight.

rows.title: Cantero v. Bank of America — SCOTUS 22-529 (2024); 2d Cir. on remand; new petition No. 25-1313
cells: When does a federal bank charter preempt state financial law?
2024: nuanced Barnett-Bank "significant interference" test, no categorical preemption. On remand the bank won again (2026-05-05); a second cert petition is pending.
The method that will decide the GENIUS-era fights — whether a federal stablecoin charter displaces state money-transmission, reserve, and consumer rules.

rows.title: Van Loon v. Treasury/OFAC — W.D. Tex.; 5th Cir. 23-50669 (2024)
cells: Are immutable smart contracts "property" of a sanctioned person under IEEPA?
Fifth Circuit: no — immutable code can't be owned or controlled. Treasury delisted Tornado Cash 2025-03-21; the case ended after remand.
The first judicial boundary on sanctioning code itself: OFAC keeps power over people and mutable property, but the protocol layer slipped the blocklist.

rows.title: Coin Center v. Treasury — N.D. Fla.; 11th Cir. 23-13698
cells: Parallel Tornado Cash challenge — property theory plus First Amendment claims.
Argued 2024-11-19; Treasury's delisting changed the operative state mid-appeal.
The twin that never got its own holding — mootness by agency retreat, a pattern this map sees repeatedly.

rows.title: Culley v. Marshall — SCOTUS 22-585 (2024)
cells: Does due process require a separate preliminary hearing while seized property awaits forfeiture trial?
No — a timely merits hearing suffices (6–3).
The state may hold what it seizes for the duration. Applied to digital assets, custody-pending-forfeiture is the whole game (see JM-36).

rows.title: United States v. Gratkowski — 5th Cir. 19-50492 (2020)
cells: Any Fourth Amendment privacy in public blockchain data or exchange KYC records?
No — blockchain is public; Coinbase records analogized to bank records under Miller.
The tracing pipeline (analytics → exchange records → person) is constitutionally frictionless — unless Chatrie's logic (JM-24) someday reaches it.

rows.title: United States v. Approximately 69,370 Bitcoin — N.D. Cal.; 9th Cir.; cert denied 2024
cells: Who owns the Silk Road wallet the government seized?
Competing claims stricken for lack of proof; government custody stands. No source proves the wallet entered the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve.
The largest single BTC hoard in federal hands cleared its ownership contest — the reserve's supply chain runs through forfeiture standing doctrine.

rows.title: In re Celsius Network — Bankr. S.D.N.Y. 22-10964 (2023)
cells: Did Earn-account customers or the estate own the deposited crypto?
Terms of use transferred title — Earn assets are estate property; customers hold unsecured claims. Plan effective 2024-01-31.
"Your keys" ended at the click-wrap. The ruling that made custody terms the whole ballgame for every yield platform.

rows.title: In re BlockFi / Meghji v. United States — Bankr. D.N.J. 22-19361; Adv. 23-01144
cells: Customer wallets vs. estate; then estate vs. criminal forfeiture (the FTX collision).

Qualifying Wallet assets = customer property (opposite of Celsius, different terms); government limited to defendants' traceable interests; $35M+ restrained during tracing; final allocation unverified.
Fine print decides whose coins survive a collapse — and when DOJ forfeiture meets a bankruptcy estate, the bankruptcy court holds the boundary.
